note: forward_med_test and med-not-propagated-across-as.ci assert attribute 4 stripped toward a plain eBGP peer; negatives keep it toward iBGP, RS clients and for a locally originated metric (med-locally-set-reaches-peer.ci). Rejudged 2026-10-31 by an independent reader after 2fadac201c, which added only a bgp-level filter { import { final accept; } export { final accept; } } so RFC 8212 default-reject stops refusing the route on its EBGP peer; no expect line or RFC tag changed, and the filter has no refs and no modify, so it cannot touch MED. RFC 4271 Section 5.1.4: "The MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute received from a neighboring AS MUST NOT be propagated to other neighboring ASes." Break evidence (go -overlay against HEAD, ./le test bgp plugin med-locally-set-reaches-peer): green unbroken; RED with "MED: 100 (missing)" when buildRIBRouteUpdate (reactor/peer_rib_routes.go) keeps MED only on iBGP, i.e. a blanket strip of attribute 4 toward external peers, which is the over-reaction this negative exists to catch. A stack probe showed the originated route reaches the wire through Peer.sendInitialRoutes -> buildRIBRouteUpdate, NOT writeAnnounceUpdate as the .ci header comment says; eBGP strips in writeAnnounceUpdate, BuildUnicast and planBatchAttrs all stayed green. The assertion stands; the header comment names the wrong rail, and this negative covers only the queued initial-send rail, not an announce to an already Established peer. Same rejudge covers med-not-propagated-across-as.ci, whose unit f8f7628bdf changed the same way (bgp-level final-accept filter only, expects and tags unchanged): green unbroken; RED with "MED: 100 (unexpected)" at the plain eBGP receiver when applyFactsMED (reactor/forward_med.go) never records the Suppress (positive), and RED with "MED: 100 (missing)" at the RS client when medPropagationAllowedTo ignores rsClient (negative). The Go tagged units are byte-identical to the recorded ones. Verdict stands.
